requirement: The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that invokes `habeas::validate()` against its own project, so its own requirements and evidence are checked recursively by `cargo test`.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The Habeas crate MUST have a Cargo integration test that calls `habeas::validate()` against its own project. That way, `cargo test` checks the crate's own requirements and evidence.

`tests/habeas.rs#fn[habeas]` is a `#[test]` in the `tests/` directory, so Cargo builds it as an integration test. It carries the `{test}` reference to `requirements.integration.self_test`. It calls `habeas::validate()` directly.

The test needs no further assertion. I read `src/lib.rs#fn[validate]` only to see how a failure would surface. It finds the project root from the current directory, which `cargo test` sets to the crate root. It then runs `validate_repository` and panics with every validation error if the report contains any. So a failure in the crate's own requirements or evidence fails the test.

The requirement states no boundaries, modes or failure cases beyond this. How `validate` itself behaves is covered by `requirements.integration.validate`, not here. I found no gaps.
